encode-and-decode-strings.title: Encode and Decode Strings
encode-and-decode-strings.html:
Design an algorithm to encode a list of strings into a single string, and decode that string back into the original list.

Implement two methods on Solution:

def encode(self, strs: List[str]) -> str
def decode(self, s: str) -> List[str]

The encoded string is passed straight to decode, which must return exactly the original list — same strings, same order.

The strings may contain any characters, including whatever separator you pick and digits. A delimiter alone is not enough; you need a scheme that survives its own delimiter appearing inside the data.

Examples

Input: ["Hello", "World"]
Output: ["Hello", "World"]
Input: [""]
Output: [""]

walls-and-gates.title: Walls and Gates
walls-and-gates.html:
You are given an m x n grid rooms, where each cell is one of:

  • -1 — a wall or obstacle
  • 0 — a gate
  • 2147483647 — an empty room (231 - 1, treated as infinity)

Fill every empty room with the distance to its nearest gate, counting steps up, down, left and right. If no gate can reach a room, leave it as 2147483647.

Modify rooms in place; the return value is ignored.

Examples

Input: [[2147483647, -1, 0, 2147483647], [2147483647, 2147483647, 2147483647, -1], [2147483647, -1, 2147483647, -1], [0, -1, 2147483647, 2147483647]]
Output: [[3, -1, 0, 1], [2, 2, 1, -1], [1, -1, 2, -1], [0, -1, 3, 4]]
Input: [[-1]]
Output: [[-1]]

number-of-connected-components-in-an-und.title: Number of Connected Components in an Undirected Graph
number-of-connected-components-in-an-und.html:
You have a graph of n nodes labelled 0 to n - 1, and a list edges where edges[i] = [a, b] is an undirected edge between a and b.

Return the number of connected components in the graph.

A node with no edges is a component on its own.

Examples

Input: 5, [[0, 1], [1, 2], [3, 4]]
Output: 2
Input: 5, [[0, 1], [1, 2], [2, 3], [3, 4]]
Output: 1

graph-valid-tree.title: Graph Valid Tree
graph-valid-tree.html:
You have n nodes labelled 0 to n - 1 and a list of undirected edges.

Return true if these edges form a valid tree.

A valid tree is connected — every node reachable from every other — and has no cycles. Both conditions matter: n - 1 edges alone does not make a tree if some of them form a cycle and leave a node stranded.

Examples

Input: 5, [[0, 1], [0, 2], [0, 3], [1, 4]]
Output: true
Input: 5, [[0, 1], [1, 2], [2, 3], [1, 3], [1, 4]]
Output: false

alien-dictionary.title: Alien Dictionary
alien-dictionary.html:
An alien language uses the English letters, but in an unknown order. You are given a list of words that is sorted lexicographically by that unknown order.

Return a string of the language's letters in order. If several orders are consistent with the words, return any of them. If the words contradict themselves, return "".

One contradiction is easy to miss: if a word comes before its own prefix — ["abc", "ab"] — no ordering can explain it.

Examples

Input: ["wrt", "wrf", "er", "ett", "rftt"]
Output: "wertf"
Input: ["z", "x"]
Output: "zx"

meeting-rooms.title: Meeting Rooms
meeting-rooms.html:
Given an array of meeting time intervals, where intervals[i] = [start, end], return true if a person could attend all of them.

Two meetings clash if they overlap. A meeting ending exactly when the next begins is not a clash, so [0, 5] and [5, 10] are fine.

Examples

Input: [[0, 30], [5, 10], [15, 20]]
Output: false
Input: [[7, 10], [2, 4]]
Output: true

meeting-rooms-ii.title: Meeting Rooms II
meeting-rooms-ii.html:
Given an array of meeting time intervals, where intervals[i] = [start, end], return the minimum number of conference rooms required to hold them all.

This is the largest number of meetings running at any one instant. As above, a meeting ending exactly when another starts does not need a second room.

Examples

Input: [[0, 30], [5, 10], [15, 20]]
Output: 2
Input: [[7, 10], [2, 4]]
Output: 1
